Computer System Design and Related Services

merger_description:
Visa, Inc., through its indirect wholly owned subsidiary, Visa Open Connect Limited (**Visa**) intends to acquire all of the shares in BioCatch Ltd (**BioCatch**) (the **Acquisition**).

Visa is a global payments technology company that supplies payment products and services and commercial and money movement solutions. Visa also offers services designed to support and enhance payments, including fraud, authentication, authorisation, tokenisation, and risk management solutions. Its fraud and risk solutions are primarily marketed under the ‘Visa Protect’ brand. It also offers risk solutions for account-to-account payments through ‘Visa Protect Account to Account’, which helps financial institutions detect and prevent payment fraud and scams.

BioCatch is an Israeli security software company with operations globally. It supplies software solutions that discern different users’ patterns of behaviour on devices to identify cyber threats in real-time by analysing patterns of behaviour across online and mobile applications and deviations in that behaviour. Its technology uses machine learning to monitor various behavioural parameters to detect anomalies suggesting compromised access by bots, fraudsters, and remote access tools.

determination_table_content.details:
When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form, information from third parties, and publicly
available information.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition would be unlikely to have
the effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings:
• There is limited horizontal overlap between Visa and
BioCatch and the parties are not close competitors.
• Post acquisition, Visa would not have the ability and
incentive to foreclose rivals through linking behavioural
biometrics with payment services or other fraud prevention
solutions. This is due to the availability of alternative
suppliers of behavioural biometric software and other fraud
prevention solutions.
Concerns were raised regarding the potential competitive impact of
Visa’s access to the data held by BioCatch post-acquisition. The
ACCC has considered the impact of access to such data and
considers this is unlikely to result in a substantial lessening of
competition in any market. While such data may be commercially
valuable, there are alternative sources of data which would remain
available to Visa’s rivals post acquisition.
